newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Culligan sets new marketing push.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Culligan sets new marketing push.

text.p: Culligan Water Technologies Inc, which last year focused on acquisitions and forging international joint ventures, said Thursday it will concentrate this year on marketing its new consumer product line through retail chains for the first time.

"Nine months ago, we weren't in the retail consumer marketplace," Douglas Pertz, Culligan's president and chief operating officer, told Reuters. "Next year it will be well into the $20-million-plus range from a 'zero' business less than a year ago."
Pertz said the Northbrook, Ill.-based company would expand distribution of its recently launched consumer products, such as a faucet-mounted water filtration system.
Culligan will offer the products through mass retailers like Wal-Mart Stores Inc, department stores, do-it-yourself stores like Home Depot Inc and even plumbing supply dealers.

Pertz said the company would announce an agreement this weekend with a large faucet manufacturer to integrate Culligan's water filtration technology as part of the next generation of the manufacturer's faucet line. He did not name the manufacturer.
Culligan is in negotiations on a similar original equipment manufacturing agreement with a major appliance maker, which he also declined to name.
Pertz said Culligan is also preparing to announce a joint venture in India, similar to its other joint ventures in Egypt, West Bank/Gaza, Dubai, Australia and Turkey.

Pertz said the company did studies in the first half of last year and discovered that it had the number-one brand in the marketplace in terms of recognition, even though the company's products were not sold through retail outlets.
"We focused heavily last year on distribution acquisitions," he said. "We probably added close to $15 million in dealer distribution acquisitions last year."
Culligan reported a profit of $0.37 a share in the third quarter ended October 31, up from a loss of $0.27 a year earlier.
Pertz said the company is comfortable with analysts' earnings estimates of $0.37 a share in the fourth quarter ending January 31, 1997.
"Domestically, this is a $15 billion market that we just participate in," Pertz said. "There's a lot of room for growth, there a lot of room for players."
